title: Accuracy vs. Precision

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Accuracy is how close a measurement is to the true value. Precision is how close repeated measurements are to each other, regardless of whether they are close to the true value.
explanation: A method can be precise but not accurate (consistently wrong in the same direction, e.g. a mis-calibrated pipette or balance), accurate but not precise (results scatter around the true value but average close to it), both, or neither. In lab work, both matter: calibration and technique consistency (e.g. consistent pipetting angle and depth) improve precision, while proper instrument calibration and validated methods improve accuracy.

comparison.left: Accuracy: closeness to the true/target value
comparison.right: Precision: closeness of repeated results to each other

comparison.left: Calibration, validated methods, correcting systematic error

commonMisconceptions: Using 'accurate' and 'precise' interchangeably in casual lab speech.
